neighbours.label: the approximating hedge 'pretty much' / 'more or less' (fires on 'much' / 'less')
fire: After the move, our old neighbor pretty much stopped calling us.
The new phone is pretty much the same as last year's model.
By midnight the guests had more or less finished the cake.
Her grandfather pretty much built that house with his own hands.
The plan worked more or less the way we had hoped it would.
At this point the software pretty much runs itself every night.
The two candidates hold more or less identical views on taxes.
Honestly, the kids pretty much ignored the vegetables at dinner.
quiet: After the move, our old neighbor called us much less often.
The new phone costs much more than last year's model.
By midnight the guests had eaten less than half the cake.
Her grandfather spent much of his life building that house.
The plan worked much better than we had hoped it would.
At this point the software needs less maintenance every night.
The two candidates disagree very much about taxes.
Honestly, the kids ate less of the vegetables at dinner than usual.
